page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-192-lssd is an x86_64 instance powered by a 96-core Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, providing 192 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. The server includes 504 MB of L3 cache, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core. Memory allocation totals 1488 GB of RAM, equating to 7.75 GB per core. The instance is bundled with 12864 GB of local NVMe solid-state storage across 32 drives, providing low-latency ephemeral I/O. Hardware-level acceleration includes AVX-512, Intel AMX tile and int8 execution units, and cryptographic vector enhancements. No discrete GPUs are provisioned.

Benchmark evaluations position this configuration in the top 10 percent of servers for multi-core compute and data throughput. In stress-ng multi-core testing, the instance achieved a score of 208068.3, complemented by a PassMark CPU score of 154470.87. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 711.54 GB/sec on 256 MB blocks, while cached 16 KB read throughput exceeds 15353 GB/sec. The instance delivers high transaction rates, achieving over 313 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and top-tier metrics across PassMark database operations, Clang compilation, and multi-threaded decompression workloads.

The dense pairing of 192 vCPUs, nearly 1.5 TB of system memory, and over 12 TB of high-speed local NVMe capacity provides high hardware consolidation efficiency for storage- and memory-bound operations. The absence of GPU accelerators makes it unsuitable for heavy model training, yet integrated AMX and AVX-512 capabilities maintain strong prompt-processing throughput for large CPU-based language models. Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-192-lssd is best configured for large in-memory database clusters, distributed caching tiers, real-time analytics, and high-concurrency transactional database engines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-192-lssd is an x86_64 instance featuring 192 dedicated vCPUs from a 96-core Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor running at 2.3 GHz. The platform is configured with 1488 GB of system memory, yielding 7.75 GB per core, and is bundled with 12864 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across 32 drives. It contains 504 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, without discrete GPUs. In synthetic evaluations, the instance ranks in the top decile for stress-ng multi-core compute, large-block memory read bandwidth at 711.54 GB/sec, and database operations. Redis SET testing exceeded 313 million operations per second. The substantial memory density and bundled local high-speed NVMe storage make this server well suited for large distributed in-memory databases, high-throughput caching layers, ETL pipelines, and high-concurrency enterprise workloads.
